<r>Te Deum</r>
<c>T</c>e Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.
Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.
Tibi omnes Ángeli, * tibi Cæli, et univérsæ Potestátes:
Tibi Chérubim et Séraphim * incessábili voce proclámant:
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
Pleni sunt cæli et terra * maiestátis glóriæ tuæ.
Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
Patrem * imménsæ maiestátis;
Venerándum tuum verum * et únicum Fílium;
Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.
Tu Rex glóriæ, * Christe.
Tu Patris * sempitérnus es Fílius.
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.
Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
Iudex créderis * esse ventúrus.
<n>(Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus)</n> Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
<n>(Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem)</n> Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.

b.d26d67c2bb:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>T</c>értio Kaléndas Ianuárii Luna secúnda. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>R</h>omæ natális sancti Felícis Primi, Papæ et Mártyris, qui sub Aureliáno Príncipe Ecclésiam rexit. Ipsíus tamen festum tértio Kaléndas Iúnii celebrátur.
<h>S</h>poléti item natális sanctórum Mártyrum Sabíni, Assisiénsis Epíscopi, atque Exsuperántii et Marcélli Diaconórum, ac Venustiáni Prǽsidis cum uxóre et fíliis, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre. Ex ipsis Marcéllus et Exsuperántius, primum equúleo suspénsi, deínde fústibus gráviter mactáti, postrémum, abrási úngulis et láterum exustióne assáti, martýrium complevérunt; Venustiánus autem non multo post, simul cum uxóre et fíliis, est gládio necátus; sanctus vero Sabínus, post detruncatiónem mánuum et diútinam cárceris maceratiónem, ad mortem usque cæsus est. Horum martýrium, licet divérso exstíterit témpore, una tamen die recólitur.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ sanctórum Mansuéti, Sevéri, Appiáni, Donáti, Honórii et Sociórum Mártyrum.
<h>T</h>hessalonícæ sanctæ Anýsiæ Mártyris.
<h>I</h>bídem sancti Anýsii, eiúsdem civitátis Epíscopi.
<h>M</h>edioláni sancti Eugénii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>R</h>avénnæ sancti Libérii Epíscopi.
<h>A</h>quilæ, in Vestínis, sancti Rainérii Epíscopi.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.08ff9a9dd3:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>D</c>ecember 30th 2027, the 2nd day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, the birthday of St. Felix I, pope and martyr, who governed the Church during the reign of Emperor Aurelian. His feast day is celebrated on the 30th of May.
<h>A</h>t Spoleto, under the Emperor Maximian, the holy martyrs Sabinus, bishop of that see; the deacons Exuperantius and Marcellus, and the President Venustian along with his wife and children. Marcellus and Exuperantius were first racked then heavily cudgelled, then mangled with hooks, and their sides were afterwards burnt until they died. Venustian and his wife and children were shortly afterward put to the sword holy Sabinus had his hands cut off, and was long imprisoned, and at length lashed to death. These did not all suffer at the same time, but they are all commemorated upon the same day.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, the holy martyrs Mansuetus, Severus, Appian, Donatus, Honorius and their companions.
<h>A</h>t Thessalonica, the holy martyr Anysia (about the year 303).
<h>T</h>here likewise holy Anysius, bishop of that city. (He succeeded St. Ascole, and died about the year 404.)
<h>A</h>t Milan, the holy confessor Eugenius, bishop of that city.
<h>A</h>t Ravenna, holy Liberius, bishop of that city.
<h>A</h>t Aquila, in the Abruzzi, holy Rainerius, bishop of that city (in the twelfth century).
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
